summary: air carrier technician reported during a field trip they ordered a part but failed to order the safety equipment required to accomplish the work.

the flight crew of a corporate cl-605 cleared via the riivr star to lax was caught short when approach control advised them to expect runway 24r vice 25l as depicted on the arrival. difficulty reprogramming the fms for the new ils resulted in autoflight remaining in vnav path and the aircraft leveled at 14;000 feet instead of expediting to 10;000 feet as requested by approach.
light sport aircraft pilot reported a helicopter took off over him with about a 50 foot clearance while he was taxiing at ffz airport.
gulfstream vi pilot reported discrepancies in clearances received via cpdlc.
attempting to taxi into the gate in tight ramp quarters the widebody air carrier aircraft's jet blast moved two cargo 'cans'; damaging one.
a helicopter pilot orbiting at 1;000 ft north of zzz with two other helicopters; reported a near miss with an apparently military uh-60 which transited north out the area without communicating.
b777 plt inadvertently operates the acft after his 60 birthday.

pa-28 pilot reported experiencing engine rpm issues during climb to begin an ils approach.  reporter stated reducing the throttle stopped the engine rpm oscillations and they were able to divert to the best suitable airport.  reportedly; the spring clip that secures the cable to the pivot bolt had come loose which caused the propeller control cable to detach resulting in the engine rpm issues.
sr22 pilot reported that the exhaust manifold pipe fell off during climb.
beechcraft pilot reported a near-midair-collision after takeoff from 6b6 non-towered airport.
government uas pilot reported a loss of control while conducting indoor training which caused the uas to crash.
air carrier flight crew reported an autopilot malfunction during approach resulted in early descent and low altitude alert from atc.
c310 pilot reported a total electrical failure inbound to hum that resulted in an msy mode c veil transponder violation.
an md80 crew on the dfw triss2/txk was flying direct txk after a direct triss clrnc because the intervening waypoints were dropped from the fms. atc redirected rte.

b737 flight crew reports losing control while taxiing in icy conditions with a strong quartering tailwind. the aircraft rotates right initially; then sharply to the left as the nose wheels find traction and turns 180 degrees before stopping. the crew returns to the gate for a maintenance inspection and eventually an aircraft swap.
crj-200 maintenance technician reported previous maintenance discrepancies on flap components.
b757 flt crew reports engine surge/stall during climb at fl190; declares emergency; complies with qrh; and diverts to nearest suitable arpt.
tower controller reported an aircraft did not follow taxi instructions and caused a runway incursion.
b777 flight crew reported an engine malfunction resulting in a rejected takeoff.
air carrier pilot reported being advised by flight attendants during taxi out that passengers were not complying with face mask policy.

Following departure from Philadelphia, a high frequency whistling noise was heard and inspection revealed an escape of air at the lower aft corner of the rear service door. Pillow cases were placed in this area to reduce the air noise but no further action was taken. While the aircraft was descending through 4,000 feet the door blew out. The ensuing outward rush of air ejected a flight attendant who was near the door opening. Undetected insecure latching of the rear service door, resulting in an inflight explosive decompression which ejected a flight attendant from the aircraft.
center controller reported a heavy workload with congested airspace led to an aircraft descending below the minimum ifr altitude.
b737-700 flt crew fail to take note of revision to the pdc clrnc. fly sid vice loc course as directed by that note on departure.
a flight crew landed on sfo runway 28l with a clearance to expedite via taxiway d; but exited on taxiway t because of confusing signage and lighting.
a b757 captain taxiied onto runway 8r after leaving the ramp and mistaking taxiway mike for november and so then believing runway 8r was taxiway m.
b767-300 is concerned regarding the company eng out procs.
e190 captain reports striking novelty balloons on final approach.
a be1900 flight crew stopped safely on the runway after suffering two flat main gear tires following a landing in gusty crosswind conditions.
a b737-700 technician rpts possible failure to install 2 bolts and 2 washers on the horiz stabilizer jackscrew fail safe lug. this rpt involved 3 acft.
pa-24 pilot reported landing gear extension problems on approach. a go around was executed and several low passes performed while manually extending the landing gear.
pilot monitoring reported pilot in command lost control while landing in a crosswind.
flight crew reported #1 thrust reverser deployed at 500 ft. on departure. crew shut engine down per reverser deployed' checklist and returned to field.
cessna 182 pilot reported landing on a country road due to inadvertently selecting the 'off' position with the fuel selector valve.

a flight crew entered the pdc ase clearance in the fms then changed the arrival to a visual; but did not they realize until atc questioned their track that the visual approach programming caused two fixes to drop from the routing.
pilots reported losing control of the aircraft after landing and sliding off the runway.
air carrier captain reported some new max 737 planes do not hold programmed descent airspeed. reporter stated the new max 737 aircraft begin to slow early while descending.
a ce560xl flight crew flew through an altitude restriction on the teb 5 departure.
an a320 crew rpts that because no ndb receiver is installed in this acft type; they could not comply with an eng out proc at rno requiring nav to an ndb.
b737 captain reported a dual fms failure resulted in a diversion.

the flight crew of a large transport reported that the recent implementation of a new before takeoff checklist resulted in greatly reduced situational awareness by the pilot performing the checklist; and increased the potential for taxi conflicts or mishaps.

captain reports that after takeoff; at 400 ft; he noticed the left epr became erractic and oscillating including the left n1 tach; followed by several bangs. throttle reduced to idle and banging noise stopped. air turnback accomplished. left engine inlet bullet found separated from engine and resting in the inlet nacelle.
j3 cub pilot reported their engine lost power on initial climb and they returned to the departure airport.

an air carrier check airman noted that lost communications procedures written 40 years ago and not updated since are difficult to correctly apply to the complex stars designed for 'descend via' clearances.
a center controller reported an aircraft deviated from its assigned holding direction and flew below the minimum ifr altitude.

an air carrier captain reported they were holding short of a taxiway waiting for an aircraft to pass when they observed a different aircraft taxiing across their path that would not have room to clear their aircraft. the reporter instructed the other aircraft to stop on ground control frequency.
a pilot reported confusion on the frequency due to similar sounding call signs.
embraer legacy 450/500 pilot reported on short final they observed a c172 still on the runway. they advised atc who changed their clearance to the parallel runway.
beechcraft baron pilot reported diverting to a nearby suitable airport after an engine that had been intentionally feathered for training would not unfeather.
md-80 captain reported he failed to properly position the fuel pump switches in a non-standard fuel load situation.
e145 first officer reported the nose landing gear door had opened during cruise. the flight crew diverted; lowered the gear and landed safely.

while intercepting the localizer; a b737-700 experienced uncommanded pitch and autothrottle anomalies.  the event was apparently related to the inappropriate capture of the glideslope from below and a short lived low airspeed deviation ensued.
air carrier flight crew reported receiving an aircraft terrain alert during approach. flight crew corrected aircraft altitude and continued approach.
two flight attendants reported having to work a flight a few days later after being on a flight with a passenger who had tested positive for covid-19.
a b757-200 lndg gear ctl module was replaced with no gear swing required. gear pins were installed and removed but required inspection for pin installation and removal not documented.

msp tower controller reported tracon instructions to an arrival caused an unstable approach and a go-around. the tower controller stated that tracon issued the instructions to comply with the new converging runway operations (cro) procedures at msp; but the tower controller sees the procedures as unsafe as many factors are not included in cro. the controller indicated the procedures do not provide controllers the capability to ensure positive separation of aircraft.

b757 captain notes that the glideslope to runway 23 at buf is unusable beyond 5 degrees right of the loc and may be dangerous when flying a coupled approach. suggests that stronger language and procedure modification may be in order for this runway in the tailored briefing pages.
light aircraft instructor pilot reported an nmac with a turboprop twin aircraft in the vicinity of x04 airport.
c172 instructor pilot reported an airborne conflict with another light aircraft in the traffic pattern on the downwind leg at bvy.
tailwheel flight instructor reported that the student lost control during landing that resulted in contact with a runway sign.
b767 flight crew experienced an unscheduled stab trim passing fl260 during climb. after complying with qrh procedures crew elected to return to the departure airport for an overweight landing.

a check airman conducting initial operating experience with a new first officer on a crj-700 was distracted by other duties as the first officer; who was flying a visual approach to bhm; got distracted; overturned to final and triggered a low altitude alert from the tower and a momentary egpws warning. an appropriate profile to an uneventful landing was quickly re-established and no go around resulted.

tower controller described a loss of runway separation event when changing a 'land long' approval to an 'exit the runway' clearance with a hold short clearance; the hold short instruction confused by all involved.
experimental pilot climbs into class a airspace without a clearance as a result of weather.

a pilot in a king air was distracted during a maintenance flight with a mechanic; and neglected to activate the auto ignition switches. when he noticed; he reached for the switches but unintentionally activated the starter generators; removing generator power from the electrical system. after a successful return to the departure airport; he discovered that his radio was unable to contact ground control; likely due to the exhaustion of the battery power.
pa32 pilot reported executing a go-around after losing communication and navigation radios on approach. during the go-around; there were track and altitude deviations.
a b737-700 maint ctlr was advised #2 vhf radio was inop. sent station directions for reracking transceiver. actual rpt was #2 ils inop. unit was reracked and chked ok. no cat i downgrade performed.
captain reported ramp personnel notified flight crew that a battery powered passenger bag was illegally transported in cargo compartment.
captain reported gps jamming at this location.
b757 flt crew has a track hdg dev during mia dep from mia.
a320 captain explains the reasoning behind his rejection of an aircraft for a flight to a caribbean island with a non-functional pa system.
pilot reported experiencing a track heading deviation and cited rustiness and lack of flying as a contributing factor.
a b737-800 first officer immediately shut down the right engine when he noted the forward cargo door was being opened by ground crew prior to setting the parking brake and shutting down the engines.
captain reported loss of the left air data computer in cruise. this caused unreliable airspeed indications. the flight crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
flt crew of b757 notified of dangerous goods on board after tkof.
an md80 cabin attendant rpts in cruise the aft cabin halon fire extinguisher spontaneously began spraying. wrapped in blanket and placed in locked lavatory.
b737 captain reported speed trim light fail light illuminated in flight. flight continued to destination.

ifr citation landing hnd; vectored by l30 tracon; experienced conflict at 6300 with issued vfr traffic; executed emergency climb; reporter claiming atc's decision to issue decent clearance into known traffic was a safety issue.

b737-800 flight crew report discovering in cruise that their control column can be moved freely about eight inches fore and aft; without disturbing the autopilot or producing elevator movement. the flight continued to destination with the autopilot engaged. during a turn at 11;000 feet the autopilot becomes disengaged and cannot be reengaged. although the elevator felt soft the captain is able to manually land the aircraft.

flight instructor reported that during landing; the right main gear down and locked indicator light was inoperative. they contacted the tower; and they confirmed the gear was down so at 500 feet; they shut both engines down and landed.
sr22 pilot reported a nmac while in traffic pattern at towered airport.
air carrier flight crew reported smoke in cockpit when apu started during pre-light. flight crew shutdown apu and evacuated aircraft.
a cessna pilot reported a near miss with a drone.
b737 captain reported concern with the tight spacing in use between departures and arrivals at sna.
a b737 crew reports missing an arr crossing restriction after the fo pressed 'alt intv' thereby deleting the next fix's alt constraint.

a11 tracon controller conducting on the job training reported the trainee vectored an aircraft for sequencing below the minimum vectoring altitude.
plt of a sma inadvertently enters class b airspace while focusing on tis tfc display.

citabria pilot reported a runway excursion during a training flight after a balked landing with an instructor when confusion and communication issues resulted in opposite control inputs by the student and instructor; resulting in descending back to the runway surface and the aircraft stopping in the grass.
zhu controller reports of a loss of separation due to lack of speed control. other sector did not advise the working sector that speeds were not given/or removed to continue separation standards.
aero commander meyers 200d pilot reported the landing gear failed to extend; so the emergency unlock system was used.
traveler aa5 pilot reported a loss of throttle lever control during a practice approach resulting in a successful engine out landing.
b737-400 departs with 3000 lbs more fuel in ctr fuel tank than calculated.
amateur/home built/experimental pilot reported the nose wheel gear collapsed during landing.

a b737-500 flight crew suffered a pressurization failure; initiated an emergency descent and; when level at 10;000 feet with adequate fuel reserves; elected to continue to their destination rather than divert.
instructor and student flying a retired military training aircraft reported landing short and striking a reil light during training for a simulated engine failure.
gulfstream iv captain reported a pressurization problem that resulted in an expedited descent and precautionary landing.

air carrier captain reported a passenger was not compliant with mask policy and being disruptive. captain reported multiple interruptions during the flight in order to communicate with company about the situation.

b757-200 flight crew is surprised to see the a flight attendant entering the cockpit to check on their welfare during a night flight over the pacific.  the call bells were muted due to the handset not being in its' cradle and both pilots were wearing noise canceling headsets masking the door chimes.
crj-900 flight crew reported they descended below the level off altitude when the autopilot did not capture.
emb-145 captain reported a pitch trim anomaly during climbout.
q400 first officer questions the terminology of the approach controller who clears him for an 'ils approach; glide slope out of service' instead of a 'localizer approach.'
a b737 pilot reports an incomplete le flap mel procedure caused the stall warning to activate on tkof.
air carrier pilot reported gps jamming on approach to amm. the reporter was unsure of the procedure to follow if they had been forced to divert.
medevac helicopter pilot reported a temporary loss of control while on the ground at a landing site.

center operations manager reported center took over airspace from the tracon due to tracon frequency outages. another center controller reported an aircraft flew below the minimum terrain requirements due to the controller's lack of training and lack of published procedures to follow when center was working with unfamiliar tracon airspace.
a landing hs-125 crew was issued a taxiway exit clearance with a hold short of the parallel runway; but incurred the parallel so an aircraft taking off went nearly overhead.

an instructor pilot reported that his foreign student pilot pitched up 30 degrees while flying in heavy imc weather because he attempted to avoid weather visually without referencing attitude instruments.
zdc controller described sector closing temporarily as a result of lack of staffing; user impacts reported.
The aircraft crashed into Mt. Pan, 25 miles SW of Athens while preparing to land. The flight crew deviated from the proper track and descended below the minimum safe altitude during approach.

a320 flight crew experiences an unstable glideslope during approach to runway 16l at sea. it is ultimately determined that the tower is crossing aircraft to depart runway 16c which is causing the instability.
regional jet pilot reported experiencing an airborne conflict with an aircraft taking off from a parallel runway during an atc directed go-around.
sav controller described radar failure; claiming current analog equipment is not compatible with closely located military digital radar; which could improve sav radar's tracking performance.
b737-700 captain reported a problem with the rudder trim which eventually resulted in the flight diverting to an enroute field.

a b737-800 flight attendant was assigned an aircraft the day following a flight in the aircraft which had the dirty socks odor after engine start; on climb and again on descent. following this event; crew members had headaches; burning throats; metallic mouth taste and skin reactions. the apu was replaced.

flight attendant expressed concern that attending a scheduled recurrent training class with a group of flight attendants could increase the risk of spreading the covid-19 virus to other crew members and passengers.
emb145 flt crew had a rwy incursion at ewr.
While on approach the nose pitched up, the aircraft stalled and crashed short of the runway. Icing of the horizontal stabilizer.
air carrier captain reported it would be beneficial to have raised lighting and chart the non-movement area at dlh airport.

a mechanic and pilot report on landing a beech travel air 95 with the rt main gear not down even though they had a green landing light; a mechanical gear down and locked indication and no gear warning horn during throttle reduction.
b737 pilot reported non-standard push-back communications release procedure by ground crew.
flight attendant reported a soup canister exploded as it was being opened and resulted in burns.
c421 pilot reported a loss of engine power in cruise due to a failed throttle cable.
pa-31-350 pilot reported an inflight engine shut down due to high cylinder head temperature and low oil pressure.
b737-700 flight attendant reported the cabin was very hot during boarding and all phases of flight.

air carrier captain reported a sharp acrid odor during cruise. after conferring with dispatch the odor was determined to be caused by a volcanic ash event which was remedied by climbing to a higher altitude.
d10 controller experienced a loss of separation event when a dal departure failed to follow route instructions; the reporter claiming lack of pilot language skills caused the event.
stinson pilot reported an engine fuel starvation incident due to a stuck fuel selector valve; resulting in a forced landing at a diversionary airport.
the flight crew of an air carrier aircraft suffered multiple system indication failures; declared an emergency; and returned to their departure airport for maintenance.

a flight attendant reported feeling ill while at cruise on an out and back flight. then she was reminded that her company had pilots use pressurization low flow to save fuel. she felt better after asking for increased air flow.
citation excel pilot reported an acc door unlocked warning after takeoff and returned to departure airport as a precaution.
crj200 diverts on account of ill and disruptive pax in need of medical attention.
a pilot reported a near miss in vmc with another aircraft in class e; but not communicating with tracon.
a vfr pilot reported a nmac with a small aircraft which was not communicating on the published ctaf frequency.
crj 900 flight crew reported low altitude alert from atc and a egpws alert on approach.
tow plane plt reports parachutists are failing to abide with fars regarding clrnc from clouds resulting in conflicts with other users in the vicinity of the arpt.

zab controller reports a uav descending without clearance; causing loss of separation with a be20. the uav pilot stated he was descending in compliance with the loa. the reporter believes that uav pilots should have licenses and be properly trained to fly an ifr clearance in the nas.

a be33 nose gear collapsed on landing. the single green light indicating all three gear's position remained green.
crj flight crew reported they forgot to remove one of the pitot tube covers before takeoff but were able to continue to their destination.
sf340b flight crew reported high itt on the right engine and vibration and low power output on the left engine after takeoff. they diverted to a nearby airport and landed safely.
air carrier captain reported a loss of nose wheel steering due to hydraulic leak and the aircraft had to be towed to the gate.
b747-200 flt crew has a track hdg dev during the sulus 3s dep from eddf.

a321 flight attendant reported a fumes event which was not communicated to the entire flight attendant crew in order to provide a complete evaluation of the event. the reporter experienced health issues.
m20 pilot reported a midair collision occurred during formation flight; with minor damage to two aircraft.
tracon developmental described an airspace incursion event during a training session when traffic and complexity increased beyond his/her capabilities.
ce550 executes gar at smo when notamed rwy closure info was not available at the sector and or briefed.
rv3 pilot reported the aircraft brakes locked on landing causing loss of control and aircraft damage. pilot described difficulty interpreting ntsb rule 830.

b737-800 flight attendant reported being informed that an escape slide deployed at the gate.
cabin attendant rpts attempts by boarding agents to falsify number of children on board in order to reduce rpted togw at or below max.

b787 flight crew reported receiving nose wheel steering and no land 3 eicas messages in flight. upon landing the nose wheel steering did not work; but the crew was able to clear the aircraft off the runway with the use of differential braking.
a319 flight crew reported ground delay due to hazmat cargo improperly loaded.
an a320 found with #3 main wheel 1 tie bolt broken. replaced #3 wheel and tire assembly.

b757 pilot believes that the online training he has received concerning the extensive changes to the flight manual; profiles; call outs; normal and abnormal checklists; as well as cockpit flows; is inadequate.
air carrier first officer reported turning on the incorrect lga taxiway due to confusing signage.

r90 controller voiced concern regarding the radio coverage at cbf; suggesting that rtr frequency equipment be installed at cbf; a busy non-towered airport.
a ce560 captain reported executing a go around after an air carrier aircraft enter dal runway 13l as he was on short final for landing on that runway.
air carrier first officer reported a uav passed off the left side of the aircraft while the flight was beginning an instrument approach.
a single pilot in a cirrus sr22 aircraft describes his concerns about lower than expected fuel flow readings from a teledyne-continental engine on takeoff roll.

lead flight attendant informs captain and gate agent that two passengers are intoxicated and need to be removed from the flight. after some discussion; the lead flight attendant is pressured into taking the passengers.
a c150 lost engine power in the practice area. the instructor assumed control; declared an emergency; and was able to safely return to the airport.
erj-190 captain reported there is no guidance in the operations manual on how to deal with ice in the engine cowl aft of the inlets.

b737ng makes two go-arounds due to weather and a gpws terrain warning on the vor runway 15 approach to bdl. divert in turbulent conditions to another airport from where the flight attendants refuse to continue.
an a320 captain is concerned that required first departure tire pressure checks are not being accomplished.
a ce550 master warning light illuminated on dep with no obvious cause. while troubleshooting; the crew missed a required dep hdg change.
a pilot landing dvo reported a nmac during final approach as he executed a go around to allow traffic spacing and then discovered this hand held radio transmitter failed but the receiver was ok.
beech sierra pilot reported a tire failure on landing that resulted in a runway excursion.
late rwy change on civet star to lax results in track and alt dev by b757 flt crew.
ground employees reported concerns regarding social distancing protections in their work environment.

a newly minted private pilot on a cross country to hsv lined up on closed runway 36r vice runway 36l for landing. the tower intervened and appropriate advisories and course adjustments prevented an incident.
a320 captain reported an airspeed split on the isis display on takeoff roll. the flight crew elected to continue the flight to destination airport.
when a lear 25 pilot turned the right engine nacelle heat off after leveling and accelerating at fl410 it flamed out so during descent toward fl200 he restarted the engine and returned to fl410.
controller reported pilot failed to follow control instructions possibly due to language barrier; which resulted in entering a higher mia.
c402 pilot reported a dual alternator failure during climb resulting in a diversion to an alternate airport.
flight instructor reported the student lost directional control during takeoff.

a md-80's right engine was producing little to no thrust during climb; so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport where arff found leaking fuel. they directed an engine and apu shutdown.
heavy cargo acft lndg gear failed to retract after tkof. flt returned to dep arpt.
bonanza pilot reported being distracted by conversation with a passenger and forgot to lower the landing gear.
The right outboard flap of the plane hit the approach lights of Runway 31. The right main landing gear collapsed and the aircraft ran off the runway into the harbor.
b737-800 captain reported a flap malfunction and divert to land at the nearest suitable airport. the reporter also stated the software app to access the qrh is burdensome.
c152 student pilot and instructor reported the student executed a go-around when tower controller noticed loss of separation between the student's aircraft and another on short final.
b767 captain reported receiving final weights about an hour into the trans-atlantic flight following a takeoff that almost resulted in a tail strike.

pilot departing a non-towered airport reported they were holding short of the runway when a landing aircraft passed a few feet directly overhead.
b737 flight crew reported taking off with the wrong flap setting because of distractions.
emb175 flight crew is informed airborne that the ground crew loaded 10 bags in aft cargo hold without accounting for them on the weight and balance.

md80 captain is informed during approach by a flight attendant that there appears to be a small fire at the trailing edge of the right wing. the crew declares an emergency and lands quickly. no evidence of a fire can be detected by the fire crew after landing but sun light on residual deicing fluid is suspected as causing an optical illusion.

a general aviation pilot reported a malfunctioning alternator while inflight. he requested assistance from atc and received a traffic priority in order to expedite his arrival at the destination airport where an uneventful landing was accomplished.

air carrier captain reported the documentation for the transport of hazmat cargo had erroneous information that indicated the cargo was scheduled for a different flight and date that went unnoticed until the captain reexamined the document later in the flight.
air carrier first officer reported receiving a gpws 'pull up' warning on a visual approach to xna.
an sf340 flight crew experienced a wake encounter following an airbus on final; the aircraft rolled into a 50 degree bank before recovery and a go-around could be accomplished.
mkc controller voiced concern regarding the conflict alert (ca/ca) and it's viability; noting distractions caused by constant unnecessary alerts.
flight crew reported engine 2 oil filter bypass light illuminated on climb. the crew performed an inflight shut down; followed by an air turn back and landing at departure airport.
emb-145 flight crew reported landing gear air/ground switch failed inflight.
flight crew reported a class bravo airspace violation due to the tower being closed for covid-19 issues.
an acr pilot reports 3 atc clearances while descending to den in rapidly changing wx and missing descent crossing restrictions.
a319-100 captain reported the gate csr did not follow company policy during the final passenger boarding procedures.
b737ng captain reported that the aed (automated external defibrillator) is in a locked; non-transparent container; which does not allow flight attendants to check it during preflight.
a c150 pilot reported a tracon controller improperly applied jo7110.65; 4-2-8(d); procedure. this misapplication caused aircraft to not be provided terrain and obstacle clearance.
distr by pax conversations; pa27 plt clbs through clred alt on dep from omn.

an erj captain believed a lengthy flap overspeed that occurred after takeoff through fl180 was contributed to by untimely atc communications; fatigue and inattentive performance of after takeoff checklist by his first officer.
b37-700 flight crew reported after encountering severe turbulence and wind shear; it was decided to overfly the destination airport and divert to a maintenance base.
an unidentified air carrier jet was unable to comply with a descent crossing restriction issued late by atc. while attempting to comply the flight crew exceeded vmo for a brief period.
zdc ctlr experienced operror at fl350 as acft is clred to clb through occupied alt.
c208 captain reported an electrical malfunction and return to departure airport and noted this was the third occurrence of the same issue for this aircraft.
a319 flight crew reported they were advised of an injury when a ramp employee walked behind a running engine while the aircraft was parked at the gate.
dispatcher for regional acr alleges the company is openly posting individual dispatcher fuel usage rpts to pressure dispatchers to follow company fuel policy and minimize fuel carried.
air taxi captain reported confusing atc instructions; faded taxiway marking; and confusing intersections resulted in taxiway and runway incursions at mynn.
plt of a high performance kit acft enters cle class b while demonstrating gps nav equip to non-plt pax.
crj-900 flight crew reported a malfunctioning brake temperature monitoring system sensor caused multiple brake overheat eicas messages; requiring an air turn back.
a b757-200 fo rpts his capt's irate response when the fo told him that he would miss a civet alt constraint and directed applying forward yoke pressure.
c172 pilot reported an nmac in the pattern at non-towered gif airport; citing radio failure and aircraft misidentification as contributing.
a320 first officer reported they could not reach their destination station operations on radio frequency nor through dispatch.

a mechanic and an inspector report about factors that contributed to their mis-rigging the elevator control cable tensions on a crj-900 aircraft. the inspector was asked to train the mechanic in the tension procedure; but neither had done an actual rig of the -900 elevator cables before.

a line mechanic reported cross wiring the left main landing gear (mlg) anti-skid inboard and outboard wheel speed transducers during a field trip on a dehavilland q400. approximately three days later; the #2 main tire blew on landing due to an anti-skid issue.
pa32 pilot reported landing safely after losing one cylinder in the engine.
e145 capt rpts fms started turn towards down course fix too early on clare dep from dfw. loss of separation with other rwy dep results.
b737-400 departs from mwcr without final weight revision. overweight tkof results.
enroute controller described a probable loss of separation event during a eram testing period; the controller listed the lack of preferential settings ('pref-set') availability as one causal factor.
after losing their dc emergency bus the flight crew of an md-82 restored alternative to power to the bus via the qrh and then returned uneventfully to their departure airport for maintenance.
a b737-300 flt attendant removed the slide girt from the floor; but may not have completely stowed it. the slide fell out of the slide as the door was opened.
cl-350 first officer reported descent below crossing altitude due to autopilot mismanagement resulted in an atc alert and a cftt event.

On a flight from Houston to Dallas the airliner flew into thunderstorms. While attempting to turn around by making a right hand turn, winds lifted the port wing, forcing the starboard wing down past 90 degrees.  A stall resulted from this unusual attitude, pitching the nose down. During the recovery maneuver, the starboard wing was over-stressed, separating from the aircraft followed by the the tail and engines. The aircraft crashed into a field. Pilot's decision to penetrate a line of thunderstorms and severe weather. Visual perception of the pilot may have been reduced by a near lightning strike.
captain reported that the jeppesen flitedeck pro application obfuscates the airport operation hours are not clear and fail to reference what chart holds specific airport diagrams.

b737-800 flt crew fails to note revision to filed route when programming the fms route.
c172 flight instructor reported experiencing a rough running engine while in the traffic pattern. instructor returned and blew a main gear tire during landing.
b737-800 pilot reported right main tank overflow fuel spill during preflight.
a reserve acr pilot called in fatigued after his early duty zone schedule was changed to a late zone trip and his sleep cycle became disrupted.
pilot reported loss of engine control; resulting in an in flight shut down and a precautionary emergency landing.

an aircraft on a visual approach circling to land ase runway 33 in gusty conditions and high on approach developed an excessive rate of descent which triggered the egpws terrain pull up alert. a go-around was executed followed by a second successful visual circle to land runway 33.
cl65 flight crew reports a nmac 40 miles northeast of ric at 9;000 ft with an ultralight aircraft. evasive action was taken to avoid the aircraft laterally by 200 ft.

during a daily check inspection of an erj-190; a mechanic noticed a suspected crack on # 2 engine spinner. after performing a dye penetrant inspection; no crack was found. damaged area was reworked; signed off and aircraft departed.
pa28-235 suffers partial power loss shortly after takeoff. returns to land opposite direction at departure airport.
crj-200 first officer reported he descended below mva on a night visual to den; citing lack of situational awareness as a causal factor.
c414 plt squawks hijack vice nordo transponder code when vhf reception becomes unintelligible.
part 107 uas pilot reported learning another uas pilot had a fly away due to possible gps issue. the reporter also expressed concerns about the company's safety culture.

b737-700 captain experiences stick shaker during the turn to intercept the localizer in the clean configuration; along with intermittent bank angle annunciations; in turbulent conditions. speed had been set at clean maneuver plus five kts.
Crashed on final approach. Pilot fatigue. The pilot did not follow the recommended procedure for instrument final approach and he descended below the height prescribed in the final approach chart.

air carrier captain reported attempting to exit the runway after landing only to discover that the taxiway had been barricaded. after contacting multiple parties; airport personnel finally assisted by temporarily removing the barricades to allow the aircraft to pass through. the reporter contributed the poor lighting of the runway and taxiway environment; the lack of notams referencing the barricades; and the airport's short-staffing contributed to the event.
air carrier flight crew reported departing without knowledge the release was to an alternate destination instead of the planned destination.
c172 flight instructor reported an nmac with a pa-44 in the landing pattern.

a321 flight crew reported there was a burning smell permeating throughout the cabin during taxi and the flight attendants began to experience physiological symptoms. the aircraft returned to the gate; the passengers were deplaned; and the flight crew went to the hospital afterwards for safety reasons.
b777 captain reports deviating around weather using his emergency authority when atc clearance cannot be received in a timely manner.
acr capt reports txwy e is incorrectly labeled as txwy t on arpt diagram of mdw.
b747-200 flt crew has difficulty flying holding pattern at rolis intxn on arr to eddf.
instructor and student plts aboard c172 must reject tkof at f45 for taxiing p180 that crosses their rwy despite ctaf calls advising him to hold short.
technician reported inadequate task card and aircraft maintenance manual references; exacerbated by wrong tooling caused difficulties in purging as contaminated aircraft hydraulic system.
a321 flight crew reported recurring fume events during climb requiring flight crew to utilize 100% oxygen.
b737-400 fo rpts fatigued capt rejected a tkof at high spd due to an illuminated fuel filter bypass valve warning. rpts rejections for such anomalies are contrary to company policy.
a b737-700 was released for svc with the horiz stabilizer jackscrew fail safe lug missing the bolts and washers that thread into the lug.
air carrier captain reported that during recurring ground training individuals did not always wear a mask to protect from covid-19 exposure.
b737 flight crew reported the sjc2 sid route provides a turn that could lead into converging traffic.

b737-800 captain reported he accidentally hit the toga button on an ils approach and chose to go-around. other errors were made during the next approach before he and the first officer regained full situational awareness.

pilot reported inadvertently walking into a restricted area while attempting to cross the ramp at rdd airport. pilot also reported that signage was not lit and therefore not visible prior to entering the area.
b737-800 flight crew reported that proper procedures were not being followed during an engine start using an air cart.
emb-175 flight crew reported windshield cracking on the captain's side mid-flight resulting in a return to departure airport.
crj-200 captain and the dispatcher involved describe a return to field due to a steering inop caution message received at cruise altitude. landing is uneventful and the aircraft is towed to the gate.
ramper reports arriving at his assigned gate just after the aircraft arrives to be informed that a new ramp employee has walked behind a running engine and was knocked down.
pilot trainee with flight instructor reported loss of aircraft control on landing resulted in shutting down aircraft on the runway.
b737ng first officer reported a speed deviation occurred while they were dealing with an unreliable airspeed indicator.
a falcon 2000 first officer became distracted by a radio call and did not make the teb 8 sid 2.3 dme turn; but did turn at 2.5 dme when alerted by the non flying captain.
a319 captain reported having to brake hard to avoid a collision with a ground vehicle that drove directly in front of the aircraft while pulling into ramp.
a tracon  controller reported aircraft was issued a descent clearance; descended faster than anticipated and flew below the minimum vectoring altitude.
crj captain reported sighting of a nearby uav while on short final to lga runway 22.
an acr capt notes that a jet taxi restriction exists on ttpp's txwy west of txwy a1 but that restriction is not on the commercial arpt diagram.
a319 captain reported rejecting takeoff due to receiving a door forward cargo alert through ecam.
saab sf340b has a track/hdg dev during apch to iah.

b737-800 flight crew reported an airspeed unreliable condition during the takeoff roll. the crew stated the condition was near or through vr (rotation) and they continued. once airborne the crew completed the qrh and returned to the origin airport.

local tower controller confuses callsigns of aircraft departing on intersecting runways.  wrong aircraft takes off and the other must be cleared off their runway from position and hold to allow traffic on final to land.
flight instructor on training flight in c210 aircraft reported nmac with another aircraft.
crj200 flight crew reports strong fuel odors during approach after starting the apu for airframe deicing. apu is secured and fumes go away.
student pilot reported while executing a touch and go they lost control of the aircraft resulting in a runway excursion.

an sa227 captain reported landing in a freezing drizzle; with braking action reported as fair; to find braking action. maximum reverse and braking was not sufficient to prevent the aircraft from going off the end of the runway at a very slow speed. no damage reported.
da900 capt reports alt dev while maneuvering with tcs button depressed. reporter is new to efis and vertical tape altimeter and not aware tcs button disconnects autopilot pitch as well as roll.
a b1900d flt crew experienced a hard landing following an unstabilized approach.
an international relief officer reported extending his duty day beyond 19 hours as allowed by far 117 for a four pilot crew; then prior to landing recognizing his extreme fatigue.

a b737 crew at fl380 in level flight; experienced a loud engine report accompanied by a strong airframe vibration and surging power. they completed the engine failure qrh; declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
pa23 plt was unprepared for night flight into a busy arpt. he became disoriented; executed a missed apch; and was eventually vectored to the arpt for lndg.
light transport aircraft captain reported a track deviation due to similar sounding fix names dirrk and dirkk.
zbw controller described an airspace deviation when an ifr aircraft; cleared via flight service; failed to followed the cleared route; the reporter noting the pilot awareness was lacking.
zau ctlr experienced operror at approx 12000 ft when preceding acft slowed to an 'expected' airspd and was overtaken by succeeding tfc.
b757 first officer reported they failed to select the approach tile when cleared for approach; which led to an unstable approach and then had an altitude excursion during the subsequent go-around.
da-40 flight instructor reported an engine malfunction while climbing and returned to the airport for a landing.

ga pilot reported being stung by an unseen; unidentified insect while fueling his aircraft at poc. light-headedness and loss of unconsciousness occurred shortly thereafter and required hospitalization. he recommended at least a 30 minute delay for pilots who may be stung by an insect prior to any departure.
a boeing 737 first officer reported that after takeoff the landing gear would not retract.
emb-145 flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate after smelling smoke in the cockpit and cabin.
mia ground controllers reported a runway incursion due to the wrong tug being crossed at the wrong intersection as a departure starting to roll.
during gnd stop at ord md80 has apu fail with both engs shut down.

air carrier captain is informed by atc that his destination airport is closed by notam for snow removal. reporter and dispatcher both missed notam prior to departure. flight diverts to await reopening.
b787 flight crew reported fatigue and complacency led to an unstabilized approach; but continued to land.
Crashed into La Rodilla de la Mujer Muerta while on approach to Madrid. Loss of control due to icing and turbulence.
air carrier first officer laments the juniority and lack of adherence to regulations of some captains that she flies with.

when the crew bus from the hotel was late the layover flight attendants arrived at the airport after the crew briefing had been completed. a supervisor directed that the late flight attendants not be briefed in the interests of a timely departure. the reporter felt that the directive compromised the safety of the flight.
air carrier flight crew reported cargo compartment fire warning system malfunction.
dfw ramp controller described event when aircraft failed to contact ramp control; blocking gate entry points adding to airport congestion.
a crj200 on the second flt leg had the lower cowl of the l eng depart the acft.
pa28 pilot reported taking evasive action on departure to avoid a collision with an opposite direction aircraft not on the ctaf frequency.
air carrier flight crew reports inadvertently crossing the hold line for runway 35l at hrl due to its great distance from the runway.
a300 capt reports unsafe landing gear during approach. attempts to extend gear by alternate means are unsuccessful until problem clears up on its own and gear extends.
md-11 flight crew reported fatigue and confusion resulted in a rejected take off due to misdiagnosing a bleed air/ pack/ anti ice issue.
zab controller described a conflict event between two ifr aircraft at altitude when attention was distracted to an ifr departure in apparent conflict with prc traffic.
air carrier with zau described a very confused communications event involving four digit call signs and attempts to communicate with atc.

the failure of a pneumatic bleed valve and; thus; the loss of pneumatic anti-ice systems on a polar etops operation forced an eventual emergency landing because the flight could not be continued due to all etops diversion stations forecasting known icing conditions.
air carrier stores personnel reported notification that a mislabeled 'non-hazmat' parcel was improperly shipped.
zbw associate ctlr witnesses operror at approx fl410 when radar ctlr failed to turn conflicting acft with enough angle for separation.
flight attendant reported a passenger moved into the exit row after the briefing.  passenger was asked to move back to original seat.

general aviation flight instructor reported a near miss while in takeoff position on a runway with an aircraft turning final approach to land on the opposite runway at a non-towered airport. the pilot waited for the traffic to go around then safely performed their takeoff.

b757 flight crew reports flying a one plus hour flight with a dry ice waiver and the crew wearing co2 monitors. during engine start both monitors alert and the captain opens his window and the packs are turned on when available. the co2 concentration quickly drops to zero from .7% and the flight departs.

zse controller reported being unable to clear an aircraft's request to turn for terrain avoidance while on an approved departure procedure from rdm. the controller stated that the turn would have been below mva and the pilot told atc that this has become an ongoing issue for years.
a320 flt crew lines up with rwy 24r at cle after being vectored and cleared to land 24l. tower queries the flt crew at 500 feet and flt crew executes gar.

tecnam p2006 instructor pilot and student reported the gear pump would not turn off after the gear was extended and they received 'gear not down' message so they performed a go-around and fly by of the tower then landed successfully.
a300 flight crew reports descending below the glideslope inadvertently during a visual approach; then correcting and landing normally.
capt of unidentified acr acft declares emergency and returns to dep arpt following #2 hydraulic system failure.

b737-800 captain experiences unreliable airspeed and altimeter indications at fl380. both eec's were noted to have tripped to alternate. the captain's airspeed and the first officer's altimeter are determined to be in error and the flight is descended to fl340 where all systems return to normal.

air carrier flight crew reported being notified at destination that a notoc for hazmat payload was not on board. after further review it was determined that no notoc was provided to the flight crew at origination point.
an air carrier captain reported during a flight crew switch and cabin distractions they did not comply with a crossing restriction.
Crashed in rain, fog, windshear.  Pilot distracted as a result of a major electrical system failure. Undetected deviation from flightpath.
fractional flight crew reported the fms system on aircraft is outdated and cannot keep up with the runway changes; leading to an increased workload on the flight crew.

pa-32 pilot reported the primary navigation and communication screen went black after takeoff resulting in possible altitude and airspeed deviations. the reporter continued to destination where the avionics shop determined water damage may have caused the malfunction.

a b777 developed an apparent fuel imbalance in flight but since troubleshooting did not reveal a problem; the crew returned to the departure airport where enroute they found the fuel crossfeed valves unexpectedly open.

a line mechanic reports a b767-400 he worked earlier required an air turnback for a left main landing gear (mlg) door unsafe indication. gear door had not retracted and the bypass safety pin was still installed in the mlg door safety valve.
flt crew was issued dscnt clrnc for the apch by brazilian atc. intermediate leveloff was then given to avoid dsnding through another acft's alt.
md-82 captain reported loud; strong bird strike shortly after takeoff. wiper appeared damaged; so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to departure airport for an overweight landing.

a reserve first officer described his fatigue during a trip which has early checkin's after his body clock is prepared for his late day reserve duty time. the see-saw duty times and minimum rest are very difficult.
zbw controller reported an airborne conflict involving an ifr aircraft and a glider. notams were issued reference to the glider traffic activity.
c172 pilot reported a power loss that led to an altitude deviation that was probably related to carburetor icing.
captain reported a diversion and a precautionary landing after loss of engine oil quantity indication.
emb-145 drifted uncontrollably to the left after touchdown; striking a rwy light before control was regained.
an ac690 was advised of an incursion into russian airspace while the onboard nav showed them about 3 mi inside unites states of america airspace.
air carrier captain reported a cftt event while on the rnav runway 15 approach to dca airport resulting in a missed approach and diversion.
a b757-200 flt crew departing iad deviated from their cleared track because the fo loaded the wrong fix during preflight.
a flight instructor reported that the student pilot did not apply appropriate nose wheel steering and braking during landing rollout; which resulted in a runway excursion and minor aircraft damage.

The aircraft was 1,000 ft past the ILS touchdown point and at an altitude of 25 ft. when a loss of visual reference caused the crew to abandon their approach. The landing gear was retracted, 20 degrees flaps selected and climb power applied.  At 3,500 ft. from the threshold, in a 6 degree left bank and speed of 135 knots the No. 1 and 2 propellers struck the ground. The aircraft hit a mound of earth and broke up. Crew failed to follow approved procedures. Technique employed by the crew during abandonment of the approach under fog conditions that were not adequately reported.
an instructor pilot reported both pilots experienced carbon monoxide poisoning and returned to the airport and landed.
b777-200 experiences loss of 1 idg and the apu generator. continues to dest on domestic op.
mci ctlr expressed concern regarding supvr decision to release rwy for closure without first obtaining all pertinent info from ctlrs.

lax tower local controller and the local assist controller reported an aircraft which had been instructed to hold short of the runway taxied on to the runway at the same time a departure was beginning their takeoff roll.
challenger 350 captain reported losing n1 in the number 2 engine; resulting in a hmu [hydro mechanical unit] failure in the engine.
sf340 captain advises company flt plans do not include all fms waypoints necessary to program filed/cleared routes.
c172 plt dsnds without clrnc during apch to omn.
emb-170 captain reported a cabin alt hi light illuminated at cruise. the flight crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.

a line mechanic reports a hydraulic system accumulator bladder test performed during during an a-check revealed internal leaking of an system accumulator. three replacement hydraulic accumulators from the same vendor repair station were rejected; even though they were signed-off faa-8130 serviceable tags; before a serviceable accumulator was actually found.
a hawker 800xp departing teb on the dalton dep deviated from the charted track; in part because it was a warm day and the acft was heavy.
gulfstream giv flt crew has a track/heading and alt dev during the teb 5 rwy 1 dep.
cl601 captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to sjc in trail of a b767.
a b757 cabin crew reported very strong fumes in the acft's mid cabin. an emer was declared with a diversion. smoke dissipated during dscnt and lndg.

a mechanic references the language in the maint manual that instructs mechanic to 'loosely install clamps' while replacing the #2 cf6 eng throttle push-pull cable that may have contributed to an inflight shutdown.
a be36 pilot fixated on a frequency change to tower while descending through 2;200 ft on an ils and was notified by atc of his low altitude.
a321 captain reported a fumes event during approach descent that was described as a 'musty dirty socks'. flight crew donned o2 mask and completed a safe landing.

a government uav operated in us domestic airspace at fl270 and afterwords the controllers realized they were not provided with either the certificate of operation; pilot contact information or lost link procedures for that flight.
c172 dep from tix is clred for tkof; observes on short final; and advises atc that he or she will wait for arr tfc.

a flight attendant reports that young children cannot be properly secured in the new acro passenger seats installed on their airbus aircraft. the same seatbelts from the removed seats were reinstalled with the new seats; but will not tighten up enough to accommodate the increase curvature of the new seatbacks.

a dhc-8-200 number one engine was surging on final with the power lever at idle; so captain assumed aircraft control and attempted to feather the engine but it failed to feather. the condition lever was placed in fuel off which shut the engine down; followed by an uneventful landing.
a b737-500 acft #4 main tire was changed without installing the mlg gear pins.

a319 crew received an ecam message 'ess bus shed' passing fl340 during climb.  all electrical systems were normal; however the crew was directed by maintenance to return.  maintenance advised that the same problem had occurred a day prior.

The aircraft penetrated a flock of Whistling Swans at 6,000 ft. One, estimated to be 13 pounds, struck the leading edge of the left horizontal stabilizer, weakening the structure and causing it to detach. The aircraft lost control and broke-up in mid-air and crashed. Bird collision.

while taxiing to their hangar an instructor pilot and his student aboard a tail dragger lsa suffered a close encounter with an airport ground vehicle driven by a driver either unaware of the aircraft's presence or unwilling to abide by it's right of way on the airport.
airline captain reported an unknown individual asked the crew to release the aircraft brakes for pushback; resulting in a ramp safety issue.

an a319 flying the tyssn rnav star was leveling at 10;000 ft alt constraint * for suzsi and began slowing to 210 kts. as the 8;000 ft prino constraint was selected; the fmgc transitioned to vert spd and began a descent which the crew arrested.
chs ctlr voiced concern regarding recent change in location of operational positions; allegedly a workload and safety issue.
air carrier captain reported air traffic controller was working local; ground; and clearance delivery on one frequency resulting in communication issues and a delayed hand-off to departure control.
air carrier first officer reported being cleared for cabab but the flight crew mistakenly proceeded direct to another fix that was similar; cedab.
b767 flight crew reported they rejected takeoff due to the auto/throttle disconnect.
ce-750 flight crew reported loss of hydraulic system a on descent. crew ran the checklists; declared an emergency; and landed safely; coming to a stop with the emergency brake system.
cessna 152 instructor pilot reported a braking anomaly after landing; causing the aircraft to nearly exit the runway surface.

the distraction of the cockpit door opening at the start of the takeoff roll contributed to miscommunication between an emb-145 flight crew regarding whether or not to continue the takeoff. the pilot flying's momentary reduction of thrust triggered the spoilers and made the decision for them. after securing the door and debriefing the event; a subsequent takeoff was made without incident.
plt of c350 reports electric trim ran away to full nose down with autoplt engaged. unable to correct and landed holding manual elevator inputs to overcome the out of trim condition.
robinson r22 instructor and student; while doing night practice lndg have the helipad lights turned off during a low apch.
zdv center controller reported radio failure led to an inability to communicate and resulted in a loss of separation.
the pilot of a glastar homebuilt elected to turn directly to a nearby open field where he landed safely after his engine lost substantial power shortly after takeoff.

captain reported that the while on descent to the destination airport; the aircraft rolled 30 degrees violently in less than one second. the first officer disengaged the auto pilot and recovered from the upset attitude. the flight crew could discover no other issues and continued the approach to landing.
l1011 sustains damage to forward cargo pit when unrestrained company cargo rolls into aft wall.
a b757-200 just at rotation the flt crew felt the rudders; pedal deflection; and acft jerk l momentarily.
c182 pilot reported a taxiway incursion as well as confusion and communication issues during the interaction with atc.

a first officer questions why a partial failure of the standby power inverter on their b757-200 would not illuminate the standby power bus 'off' light during a preflight standby power test. pilot notes that without the bus light illuminating and with the ability to erase eicas status messages; flight crew could unknowingly depart with an inoperative standby inverter.
a319 flight crew reports aircraft going into alternate law shortly after takeoff. after discussion and and checklists crew elects to declare an emergency and return to departure airport.

helicopter pilot plans to land in a cul-de-sac in front of his passenger's home and checks the landing site on google earth prior to departure. upon arrival the trees appear larger than expected and an alternate landing site; further east on the same street is selected. after 15 minutes a departure is attempted but the rotor makes contact with tree branches and the helicopter is set back down.
pilot reports of violating class delta airspace while under flight following.

b767 captain experienced an eicas message; 'fwd eqmt ovht' climbing out of 18;000 ft. the qrh calls for the fwd eqmt cooling selector to be placed in standby and five minutes later the overheat message repeated. the qrh calls for the switch to be placed in override; which is successful. the crew elected to divert enroute as the aircraft is not suitable for etops.

crj200 first officer experiences a flap fail caution message during approach and goes around. an approach and landing at the current flap setting is planned and executed by the captain. the aircraft had a long history of flaps fail caution messages.
c152 executes a gar at hwo after encountering downwash from a heli.
instructor plt was accused of penetrating the washington dc adiz while executing the missed apch from fdk.
a sr22t pilot reported striking the prop and left wingtip during landing.
a pilot reported an incursion on oma runway 18 because he was looking for an engine run-up area and did not see the runway hold short lines.
b737 captain reported during climb to fl250 aircraft began to experience multiple air data systems failures; compelling flight crew to divert to make a precautionary landing.

a b737 flight crew and the tower controller involved; describe a rejected takeoff commanded by the tower controller due to the previous landing aircraft not completely clearing the runway. an aircraft on final is also sent around.
a low time small aircraft pilot entered the sac runway 20 traffic pattern incorrectly because his mental model of how the traffic pattern was constructed did not fit atc's instructions.
flt crew of a319 fail to meet xing restr.
a pa-25 aerial billboard pilot reported his release lever failed to work; and the extra drag of the billboard caused a hard landing that resulted in damage to the landing gear and prop.
c210 pilot reported an air carrier aircraft passed about 500 feet below his aircraft in the vicinity of cvg airport.
c172 plt returns to tkof arpt with rough running engine.
b757 capt reports pressurization failure after tkof and return for over weight landing.

an inexperienced private pilot in an unidentified tricycle gear airplane lost control and ground looped the aircraft while attempting to expedite his exit from the runway to facilitate the subsequent departure of an airliner holding short.
b747-400 flight crew reported returning to their departure airport after shutting down the number 1 engine because of low oil pressure and quantity.

when the b737-800 first officer disconnected the autopilot the aircraft required significant aileron input to correct for a left rolling tendency. they made a safe landing and wrote up the flight control anomaly.
b737 captain reported potentially encountering wake turbulence on approach to atl in trail of another air carrier.

an ifr b737 responded to a 'climb' ra when passing over vfr traffic previously pointed out by atc as being 500 ft below them. the controller expressed umbrage as to the flight crew's response to the ra.
maintenance technician discovered part of spoiler missing on b747-400 during post flight inspection.
an erj first officer reported that atc left the aircraft at a high altitude close to the airport which created a very steep and rapid descent.
tower controller voiced concern regarding fbo fuel truck runway crossing requests complicated because of the limited communications in the trucks.

zan controller voiced concern regarding the failure of the military to provide timely coordination with regard to the status of restricted airspace resulting in a probable technical airspace infraction.
a321 flight crew reported missing an important notam that would have precluded their approach to runway 22l at jfk; citing workload resulting from a late runway change as contributing.
b737-300 flt crew reports compressor stalls and low speed rejected tkof.

an emb-175 captain reported being advised by a flight attendant that a passenger witnessed a dark grey; spherically shaped uas three feet long flew near their aircraft's wingtip at some point during departure.
b737 captain reported sighting a drone close by the left side of his aircraft while on approach to runway 25l at lax.

air carrier pilot reported gps spoofing at cruise over the mediterranean sea while under atc control during daylight conditions. the pilot observed the aircraft at an incorrect position; which alerted the pilot to the gps spoofing event; which lasted for a short duration then resolved.
a crj700 pilot discusses his acr's resistance to additional training after transitioning to the crj. he perceived his training was inadequate.
fai ctlr voiced concern regarding mil flts when more than one acft squawks a code and the acft within the flt cause conflict alert.

b757 flt crew refuses to take large dog in the cabin due to safety concerns.
enroute controller described a loss of separation event involving several aircraft.  the reporter indicated the pilot started an unauthorized climb after being advised of the controllers' plans.
b787 captain reported receiving non-standard instructions from the ground crew; causing the aircraft to taxi over a chock and park in an improper position.
b737-800 captain reported refusing an aircraft that had several flap/slat write ups and requested a test flight before a return to revenue service.
crj-700 flight crew reported the captain accidentally pushed the left engine fire button instead of the glideslope warning cancel button on short final resulting in an unintended engine shutdown.
crj-200 flight crew reported loss of aircraft control during taxi due to nil braking action.
a sport acft landed without clearance at iag following a go around because of insufficient clrnc from tfc on landing rollout.
the single pilot of a citation lost control in turbulence and exceeded his cleared altitude by 600 ft before regaining control and returning to his assigned altitude.
the pilot of an aerobatic monoplane reported the canopy flew off during takeoff roll.
f-5at pilots reported loss of thrust on both engines during cruise. pilots were able to restart both engines and landed safely at their airport.
an ems helicopter pilot reports hospitals designating air-to-gnd ctaf freq 123.050 instead of using the faa designated air-to-air 123.025 for ga helicopters.
an enroute controller reported that an ifr aircraft was below mia and unable to hold altitude in an emergency situation due to icing.
Crashed while in a holding pattern and after running out of fuel. The crew did not follow a standard holding pattern.
acr dispatcher reports sending a crj200 back to jax with flaps failed at 30 degrees. a typo in the qrh led him to the wrong checklist. the acft should have diverted to the nearest suitable arpt.
crj-900 captain reported a track deviation resulted following a wake turbulence encounter departing phx.
b737-300 flt crew rpts jetblast during xbleed start may have caused distress to acft behind them.

b737 flight crew reported departing bwi on the conle3 to 4;000 feet. the initial heading is 285 but departure issued a heading of 090 and level at 3;000 resulting in a conflict with a c152 and a tcas ra. remaining on the conle sid would have avoided the conflict.
c172 pilot reported engine failure inflight.
a flight instructor in a c172 reported as they were executing a touch and go tower instructed them to go around due to faster air carrier traffic landing behind them.
two local controllers reported a runway incursion between a departing aircraft and a crossing vehicle.

after being cleared to cross a runway; erj crew has critical conflict with another aircraft on the far side that has failed to hold short of the intersection as instructed the morning sun was directly in the eyes of the erj crew.
an a300 flap fault ecam alerted on final as flaps 30/40 were selected. gar was initiated and a normal lndg followed the declaration of an emer.
b767-300 experiences left hydraulic system failure enroute just past pet. continued to destination.

a pilot reported his aircraft's electrical system failed during a night vmc flight beneath nyc class b near bridge ndb and although he attempted to exit the airspace; ultimately entered nearby class d as well as nyc class b.
pilot reports of confusion with pdc clearance; contacts atc and they are not able to answer the question he asks.
air carrier flight crew reported mistakes in flight release documentation relating to the number of jumpseaters on board.
b757 flt crew has a track hdg dev during dep from zspd.

air carrier flight crew reported while flying an ils approach they descended below their assigned altitude resulting in flying towards terrain. flight crew climbed the aircraft and continued the approach.
b737 flight crew reports being informed they are off track on the fissk 2 rnav to mdw due to not being aware of a notam modification to the procedure.
b757 flt crew has a close-in rwy change issued and has a tracking/hdg dev during the civet 5 arr to lax.
a line mechanic reports he was given a direct order by his supervisor to take nose landing gear (nlg) measurements on an a320 aircraft without performing a nlg strut service per the amm.
b737 captain reported an inaccurate passenger count prior to departure.
following advice of chief plt; lj55 plt suffers r main gear fire during high spd taxi tests.

a320 captain describes a fatiguing training/line check scenario beginning with a long drive for an early check in to deadhead to tncm. training/checking occurs on the return leg ending with a low fuel declaration and landing in a down pour.
c90 ctlr expressed concern regarding parallel rwy ops at ord that result in acft departing and then re-entering the class b airspace.

upon returning to the airport at the end of the flight; the instructor pilot was informed by the tower that they had been attempting to contact them on departure due to a traffic conflict with an aircraft not under tower's control.
erj-190 captain reported no flight crew dg documents [notoc] for dangerous goods loaded in cargo. flight crew executed a ground gate return to remove dg; subsequently completed an uneventful flight.
b717 flt crew encounters operational difficulties when their failure to properly interpret/understand notams for destination results in improper dispatch without a second filed alternate.
learjet 35 flight crew reported a dual tire failure during takeoff resulting in reduced braking capability during the rejected takeoff which caused the aircraft to depart the end of the runway.
